To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of social media data to assess the recreational ecosystem service provision of wetlands is feasible, even in a developing country, and 2) the recreational ecosystem service provided by the wetlands in Kerala is sensitive to changes in environmental conditions.
the recreational ecosystem services provided by wetlands in Kerala can be improved through the restoration of wetlands and by improving water quality.
(i) the recreational value of Kerala wetland ecosystems can be estimated using geotagged photographs from social media and (ii) the recreational value can be enhanced by improving water quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the application of the social media data to the analysis of ecosystem services and the management of wetland ecosystems, which are increasingly recognised to provide a wide range of services to society.
the application of crowdsourced data to inform the provision of recreational ecosystem services in the context of a developing country.
the application of social media based recreational ecosystem services (RES) modelling to inform sustainable management of wetland ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study has shown the importance of the wetlands in the state of kerala and also the importance of water quality in attracting visitors.
this study is a pioneering attempt to explore and assess the potential for using social media to understand the provision of ES and to support sustainable management of tropical ecosystems.
the use of social media for the analysis of recreational ecosystem services is a valuable tool for the management of wetland systems in developing countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed an approach to assess the provision and potential improvement of recreational ecosystem services by the network wetlands in Kerala using social media based data and that our approach is transferable to other developing regions.
social media can be used as a tool to understand the recreational value of ecosystems and to inform management and policy.
we have developed a method to estimate the recreational ES of tropical wetlands in Kerala, India, and have demonstrated that it has potential to be used as an effective tool for wetlands management.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by combining the analysis of social media data with other environmental data, it is possible to obtain a comprehensive view of the recreational ecosystem services provided by wetland ecosystems, which can be used as a tool to support the development of effective wetland management strategies.

the application of social media data in the context of environmental management is not only possible, but also provides a new and valuable perspective on ecosystem services and their potential contribution to sustainable development.
the use of crowdsourced data can be a powerful tool to inform environmental management decisions in tropical regions.
